requirement.summary: Last PIN logged-in user records lost if setup data sync from HQ to LS
requirement.description:
Prerequisites:

1. Setting PIN rules

* Location: System Management > System Configuration > User Module

* Using default is ok

2. Setting target station to use PIN login

* Location: POS System > Station Setup > Stations

* Setup name: User Login Method

>Select option "Login name and Password" and "User Pin"

3. Prepare users for using PIN

4. Assign user to target user group for PIN usage

* Location: User Management > Users group

* Include target user and / or user department

5. Setting PIN login

* Location: POS System > Ordering Setup > Config by Location

* Config Name: PIN Login Settings

* Setup name: Apply To

> Select target location accordingly

* Setup name: User List Display Info

> Select "First Name and Last Name"

* Setup name: Default Tab

> Select "Last Users"

* Setup name: User Groups Allowed to Log In by PIN

> Select target user group

6. Setting client to use "Direct Login"

* Go to client

* Revise the setup at location: General > Server Setting

* Setup name: Log-in type

> Select value "Direct connect"

Workflow

1. Click button "Direct Connect" at the initial page of the POS client

2. Click portrait icon

3. System shows Select PIN Login User page

4. Select "All Users" tab

5. System shows list of users that are allowed to log in with PIN

6. Select target user to login

7. Input the PIN

8. Click button "Enter"

9. System processes user login and displays floor plan

10. At the background, system runs sync data publish data from HQ to LS so the table recent PIN login user content is cleared

11. Click button "Exit"

12. Click portrait icon

13. System shows Select PIN Login User page

14. Select "Last Users" tab

Actual result

System shows an empty list

Expected result

System shows target user who logged in step 6 in a list
requirement.release_notes:
Bug Fixing: [Jira-66685] Last PIN logged-in user records lost if setup data sync from HQ to LS
Descriptions:
When data update is performed on a local server after the HQ server publishes setup data, the previous PIN login records on the local server are erased
Workflow
1. Go to Manage Date Release on the platform of HQ server to publish data
2. Go to Data Update on the platform of local server to download data from HQ server
3. Click the button “Direct Connect” on the initial screen of POS client
4. Click the portrait icon
5. Select “Last Users” tab
6. System displays an empty list
Expected result:
Users previously logged into the station should be displayed in the last users list
It is fixed in current version
Setup:
For detailed setup of last PIN user logins, please refer to "Infrasys_cloud_pos_release_note_1_0_73_0(Infrasys Cloud v1.2.73.0).docx"

requirement.summary: POS Report - New CUS Report "Detail Check Listing Report (with APC)" with dynamic Item Department APC columns
requirement.description:
User Story

As a report user, I want a new custom report derived from the existing Detail Check Listing Report (POS017) that adds dynamic Item Department APC (Average Per Cover) columns, so that I can view per-department sales-per-cover performance without altering the existing POS017 report.

Current Behavior

The existing Detail Check Listing Report (POS017) displays check details with its standard columns and reporting logic. It does not include any Average Per Cover (APC) calculation at the Item Department level, and there is no report variant that surfaces per-department sales-per-cover figures.

Expected Behavior

A new custom report named "Detail Check Listing Report (with APC)" is created based on POS017, keeping the existing POS017 structure, columns, and reporting logic unchanged. The new report adds dynamic APC columns for each Item Department present in the report data, calculated as Department Sales ÷ Cover Count, with corresponding APC totals. APC columns appear only at the check total and grand total levels (not on each line item), and are included in both the on-screen view and all export formats. The report is available to all users who can run any report.

Acceptance Criteria

New custom report created based on POS017

- Given the user has access to run reports

- When the user opens the report list

- Then a new custom report named 'Detail Check Listing Report (with APC)' is available

- And the existing POS017 'Detail Check Listing Report' remains unchanged and available

Dynamic Item Department APC columns

- Given a report run contains sales for specific Item Departments (e.g., Food, Soft Beverage, Alcohol)

- When the report is generated

- Then an APC column is displayed for each Item Department that has sales in the report data

- And no APC column is displayed for Item Departments with no sales in the report data

- But if a department has sales in one outlet but not another, the APC column appears only for the outlet where that department has sales

APC calculation at check total and grand total levels

- Given a check has department sales and a cover count greater than zero

- When the APC is calculated for a department

- Then the department APC equals the department sales divided by the check's total cover count

- And the APC columns appear only at the check total and grand total levels, not on each line item

- And each department's APC uses the same total cover count of the check

- But if a department has no sales on a check, its APC cell is blank or omitted rather than zero

APC handling when cover count is zero

- Given a check has a cover count of zero

- When the APC is calculated for a department on that check

- Then the APC column displays a dash (—) or 'N/A' instead of a division error

- And the report generation completes without error

APC totals

- Given a report run with APC columns generated

- When the report totals are displayed

- Then a corresponding APC total is displayed for each department APC column

- And the APC total is calculated as the sum of the individual department APC values per check

- But if a check's APC value is a dash or 'N/A' due to zero cover count, that check is excluded from the APC total sum

APC columns in on-screen view and exports

- Given the report has been generated with APC columns and totals

- When the report is exported to Excel or CSV

- Then the APC columns and totals are included in all export formats

- And the APC columns and totals are also displayed in the on-screen report view

Supporting Evidence

Region: AP

Component: Report

New Custom Report Name: Detail Check Listing Report (with APC)

Base report: POS017 – Detail Check Listing Report

APC formula: Department Sales ÷ Cover Count

APC placement: check total and grand total levels only (not on line items)

APC total: sum of individual department APC values per check

Cover count used: the check's total cover count (same for all departments)

Zero cover count: display dash (—) or 'N/A'

Exports: APC columns and totals appear in on-screen view and all export formats

Access: available to all users who can run any report

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: Q3 2025

Notes: No fixed deadline provided by the requester.

Alternatives Considered

Not provided by the requester.

Original Description (preserved by INF Prod. Studio)

Enhancement Details

- CUS Report: Detail Check Listing Report (with APC)

- based on POS017 & add new dynamic columns based on number of item department at the end

- Department APC: Sales/Cover, dynamic columns, show only departments on report with Total for each Department APC

- Column Name: Department Name APC

- Add remark on the report header: APC=Average Per Cover

_______________________________________________________________________________________________

Summary

Create a new custom report derived from the existing Detail Check Listing Report (POS017) with an additional APC (Average Per Cover) calculation for each Item Department.

The existing POS017 report structure, columns, and reporting logic should remain unchanged, with the addition of dynamic Item Department APC columns.

New Custom Report Name = Detail Check Listing Report (with APC)

1. Dynamic Item Department APC Columns

Add an APC column for each Item Department available in the report output.

The APC columns should be dynamic, meaning only the Item Departments having sales in the respective report should have a corresponding APC column.

Example:

- Outlet 1: Food + Soft Beverage

→ Food APC + Soft Beverage APC

- Outlet 2: Food + Soft Beverage + Alcohol

→ Food APC + Soft Beverage APC + Alcohol APC

The report should not display APC columns for Item Departments that are not present in the report data.

2. APC Calculation

APC should be calculated at the Item Department level using the following formula:

Department APC = Department Sales / Cover Count

Example:

- Food Sales = 1,000

- Cover Count = 2

- Food APC = 1,000 / 2 = 500

Similarly, each Item Department APC should be calculated using the respective department's sales divided by the applicable cover count.

3. APC Total

A corresponding Total should also be displayed for the APC columns, following the report's existing total structure.

The total APC should be calculated based on summing the individual APC values.

4. Acceptance Criteria

- New custom report is created based on POS017 – Detail Check Listing Report.

- Existing POS017 structure, columns, and reporting logic remain unchanged.

- APC columns are generated dynamically based on the Item Departments available in the report data.

- Each Item Department has a corresponding APC column.

- APC is calculated as: Department Sales ÷ Cover Count.

- Departments with no sales in the report are not displayed as APC columns.

- APC totals are displayed in the report.

- APC total is the sum of individual APC values.

- The APC calculation should correctly handle cases where the cover count is zero to avoid calculation/division errors.

requirement.summary: BYOD Module - Add Takeaway Box Setup - Dev
requirement.description:
Background

New function to add takeaway box to item is needed for OGS, i.e. ordering a relevant item, system auto add a takeaway box to the order.

Setup is needed in POS backend (in BYOD Module or Menu Module) and subsequently sync to OGS through menu sync.

Requirement:

1. Add Setup in POS backend

- New "Takeaway Box Setting" tab under the BYOD Module

Mock up:

- Steps to Add New

- Select "Outlet"

- Select "Item" [Within selected outlet's API Menu (POS Module-> API Settings-> Outlet Menu Settings)]: this is the takeaway box item

- Listing

- Edit Content button

- Delete button

- Name (item name of the takeaway box)

- Code (item code of the takeaway box)

- Can reference "Mix and Match Rules" page to section by outlet

Mock up:

- Can reference "Menu" page to show items bind to each takeaway box

Mock up:

- Edit the items bind to the takeaway box

- Click "Edit Content"

- Only show items within selected outlet's API Menu (POS Module-> API Settings-> Outlet Menu Settings)

- One food item cannot be mapped to more than one takeaway box

2. New API to sync the takeaway box settings to OGS

Description:
Adds Takeaway Box Settings under BYOD Management.
Set one takeaway box item per outlet, then bind foods from that outlet's API menu. One food can belong to only one box.
The list is grouped by outlet, with edit, delete, search, and expand to show bound foods.
Setup:
Deploy HERO version 1.2.115.0.
Go to [BYOD Management > Takeaway Box Settings].
On the listing page, click + beside the box name to show bound foods.
On the add page, select the outlet and the takeaway box item, then Save.
On the edit page, move foods between Available and Selected, then Save. Delete removes the box.
